frictions.description: The pacing-rules and service-availability cards have no edit control in the UI (only create + delete); the contract lists create/edit/delete, so the update clause cannot be exercised through a UI widget.
frictions.resolution: Created via UI, deleted via UI, and exercised the update with the same PUT call the client (updatePacingRule) makes, issued from the page with the UI's own token flow; labeled as browser-context XHR, not a UI control. The API half is covered by the curl group.

frictions.description: The service-availability form always submits exactly one target (target-type select), so the 400-on-zero/two-targets clause is not constructible through the form.
frictions.resolution: Sent the invalid payloads from the page with the UI's token flow: both answered 400 invalid_target. Reported as browser-context XHR, not a form submission.

frictions.description: The services create form validates time ordering client-side, so the API's 400 for invalid bounds is unreachable from the UI (no XHR is sent; an inline error appears).
frictions.resolution: Recorded the client-side guard message; the API 400 clause belongs to the curl half.

frictions.description: Special-day row action/delete buttons share one testid per date (setup-delete-special-day-2026-11-05 exists on both my row and another group's leftover row), so a testid click could delete the wrong row.
frictions.resolution: Selected rows by snapshot refs after matching the row name cell, and re-snapshotted after every re-render (refs go stale on each table reload).

frictions.description: agent-browser fill on the time inputs' shadow spinbuttons did not set values; a raw CSS-selector click on the availability Add button silently did nothing once.
frictions.resolution: Set input[type=time] values through the native value setter plus input/change events, and used scrollintoview + ref/testid clicks for the buttons.

frictions.description: The conflicts list and the block/special-day lists re-render on every mutation, invalidating agent-browser refs mid-loop; two of four delete clicks in one batch failed with 'Could not locate element'.
frictions.resolution: Re-snapshotted between clicks; final counts confirmed by sqlite.

blockers.description: VAL-SETUP-026 Re-derive clause: no mismatch exists on my assigned location, and the only real mismatch in acme is on the second location (Waterfront Kitchen, settings tz UTC vs context America/New_York), which is outside my isolation boundary; clicking Re-derive there would permanently rewrite its settings and recompute its reservation instants, and inducing a mismatch on the assigned location would alter shared time-zone interpretation while r2-book-ui runs.
blockers.quickFixAttempted: Verified the in-sync state (tzMismatch=false, no banner) on the assigned location and captured the banner rendering read-only on the existing mismatch. Did not click Re-derive (per the task's instruction not to force the mismatch).

summary: Re-tested 4 primary + 4 regression assertions on the agent-browser surface. 7 pass, 1 blocked. The round-1 fixes are confirmed: pacing-rule DELETE and service-availability DELETE now answer 200 from the UI (were 404), UI block creation on 2026-10-30 answers 201 with kind='block' occupancy expansion (area -> all 6 M1-M6 tables) and day-version bumps (was 500), and the conflicts panel renders all 8 current conflicts with confirmation code, date, party size and localized reason matching the /conflicts payload. Services CRUD + archive, turn-time buckets (incl. 400 on overlap), special-day CRUD for all four kinds with a version-bumped edit and day-version bumps, and the Sections screen show no regression. VAL-SETUP-026 is blocked only on the Re-derive click/banner-clear clause (no mismatch on the assigned location; the existing mismatch is on a location outside my boundary); the banner itself was observed rendering read-only.
